bullets.title: NVDA: Consensus beat-and-raise into earnings; OpenAI Jalapeño chip the key bear risk
bullets.body: JPM (Harlan Sur) and UBS both expect NVDA to report ~$94-95B Q2 revenue (street ~$92B) and guide $107-108B next quarter, driven by GB300/Rubin Ultra ramp. Options market implies only ~5.4% move, the lowest in 8 quarters. Key risks flagged by multiple desks: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC (co-developed with AVGO) reportedly delivers 1.5-1.9x better throughput/watt vs. GB200/GB300 at 700W vs. NVDA's 1,200-1,400W; HBM de-spec discussions (4e 8hi option); China business uncertainty; and the stock's 7-day losing streak entering the print. NVDA's 7-day losing streak was its longest in 4 years, and the stock had not had a meaningful T+1 move higher post-earnings in over 2 years.

bullets.title: INTU: Down ~9% post-earnings; JPM downgrades to Neutral, PT cut to $331
bullets.body: Intuit beat F4Q (revenue +14% YoY, EPS $4.03 vs $3.58 est) but FY27 guidance disappointed: revenue +9-10% vs +11% consensus and TurboTax growth guided to +2-3% vs +7% prior year. JPMorgan cut PT to $331 from $605 and downgraded to Neutral, citing disruption risks extending beyond TurboTax to QuickBooks. GBSG 3-year CAGR target lowered to 10-15% from 15-20%. Piper cut to Underweight (PT $290), MS EW (PT $315), UBS Neutral (PT $360), Barclays cut PT to $408. Multiple desks characterize FY27 as a deliberate reset year with EPS guide of $28.69-$28.93 (+19% YoY) driven by workforce reduction and efficiency, not revenue acceleration.

bullets.title: ORCL: Citi opens positive catalyst watch after 50%+ peak-to-trough drawdown; $330 PT
bullets.body: Citi opened a 90-day upside catalyst watch on ORCL citing extreme valuation dislocation (30% underperformance vs. large-cap tech, 50%+ drawdown described as 4-5 standard deviation event). Key catalysts: Q1 earnings expected Sep 10 and AI World investor day in late October. Citi's FY30 EPS estimate is $22 vs ~$20 consensus, with $330 PT (~18x). Separately, ORCL CDS spreads were reported to have surpassed 2008 crisis peaks, consistent with the technical selling and ATM issuance cited as drivers of the drawdown rather than fundamental deterioration.

bullets.title: META: Up ~1.3% premarket on settlement discussions in teen addiction trial
bullets.body: Meta and 29 state AGs discussed potentially settling the social-media-addiction trial, which is in its second week of an expected 8-10 week run. Meta reportedly modeled up to $1.4T in potential penalties (near market cap) if it loses, making a settlement likely far more palatable. Hedgeye's framework flips META to Bearish trend, but the settlement narrative drove the premarket bounce.

bullets.title: WSM: Big Q2 beat; comps +6.2% vs +4.5% est; raises FY guidance
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma reported Q2 EPS $2.84 vs $2.08 consensus, comps +6.2% vs +4.5% expected, and revenue $1.96B vs $1.93B est. All brands beat—WS +7.6%, West Elm +6.4%, PB +5.1%. Raised FY revenue guidance to +4.7-7.2% from +2.7-6.7% and operating margin to 17.8-18.2%. Stock has returned +31.8% since May 20 vs S&P +3.2%.

bullets.title: CIEN: Citi preview bullish; FY27 sales outlook $8.3B vs Street $8.0B; Sep 3 earnings
bullets.body: Citi expects CIEN Jul-Q sales of $1.64B (+35% YoY), marking the third consecutive quarter of 40%+ optical networking growth, with FY27 revenue forecast of $8.3B (+30.5% YoY) well above Street's $8.0B. Gross margin 45.1%, operating margin 19.8%. Dell'Oro data shows CIEN gaining share with pluggable market growing >70% YoY. $2.875B convertible offering reduced debt and boosted buybacks (~$140M).

bullets.title: MRVL: Earnings Thu Aug 27; JPM bullish on datacenter upside and GOOGL ASIC partnership
bullets.body: JPM expects MRVL to guide positively on datacenter strength, with AI custom ASIC business seen doubling to ~$4B by F28. MRVL trading at ~35x F28 EPS vs AVGO/NVDA in the teens. The GOOGL partnership expansion is described as transformational, implying ~$20B p.a. in business. Implied move in options: 8.8%.

bullets.title: AVGO: OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC partnership confirmed; Thor Ultra unveiled at Hot Chips
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm AVGO co-developed OpenAI's Jalapeño inference ASIC, which reportedly outperforms NVDA GB200/GB300 on throughput/watt and latency. AVGO also presented Thor Ultra 800GbE NIC at Hot Chips 2026 (PCIe Gen6, 5nm, 2.4B transistors, RoCEv2 offload). AVGO CDS widened +5bps to record highs, reflecting financing concerns rather than fundamental deterioration per most sell-side.

bullets.title: ANET: High-speed Ethernet demand described as near-term trading catalyst and long-duration fundamental positive
bullets.body: Hot Chips 2026 reinforced that AI factory networking is the primary bottleneck, not compute. Arista identified as primary beneficiary of high-speed Ethernet demand with positive near-term and long-term thesis. NVDA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics entered full production and its new Multiplane architecture scales to 512k GPUs at 1.6T per-GPU bandwidth.

bullets.title: BABA: Jack Ma buys $76.5M of stock; JPM maintains OW after HK$80B placement sell-off
bullets.body: Alibaba co-founders Jack Ma ($76.5M), Joseph Tsai ($20.7M), and Eddie Wu ($4.98M) bought shares after the HK$80B AI-focused placement caused an 8.4% discount and ~US$19B abnormal value repricing. JPM maintains Overweight, arguing compute infrastructure generates 22% project IRR vs ~10% cost of capital and the placement is accretive from year two at 80%+ infrastructure share. HK-listed shares gained 3%+ after the placement completed. AliCloud revenue acceleration flagged as key FY27 catalyst.

bullets.title: MSFT: Moonshot AI in talks to host Kimi K3 on Azure for up to 30% revenue share; HUMAIN AI deal
bullets.body: Moonshot AI (China) is in early-stage negotiations with Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, and Google Cloud to host its Kimi K3 model with up to 30% revenue sharing—described as potentially the first such deal between a Chinese AI developer and US cloud hyperscalers. Separately, Microsoft announced a long-term collaboration with Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN to bring Arabic AI models into the Microsoft Foundry ecosystem. Microsoft also disclosed extending data center useful lives from 15 to 25 years, shifting leases from finance to operating classification.

bullets.title: MDB: D.A. Davidson raises PT to $465 from $375; Sep 1 earnings event
bullets.body: D.A. Davidson raised MDB price target to $465 from $375 while maintaining Buy ahead of FQ2 earnings (due Sep 1). Citi also noted MDB and Sep investor day as a more important single-stock catalyst than earnings for volatility purposes.

bullets.title: SMCI: Q2 beat and raise; data center revenue guiding +45% sequential in Q3
bullets.body: Semtech (SMTC) reported Q2 EPS $0.71 vs $0.61 est and guided Q3 revenue to $410M vs $359.9M consensus, with data center expected +160% YoY in Q3. Record backlog provides >70% FY28 coverage. GS and UBS noted SMTC's data center strength as a positive read-through for the AI networking supply chain. Note: ticker in universe is SMCI (Super Micro); SMTC (Semtech) is a related but different name—SMTC is the optical networking/LoRa vendor.

bullets.title: TSEM/Semtech PT raised to $195-$230 on 160%+ YoY datacenter growth; Buy
bullets.body: UBS raised Semtech PT to $230 (from $225) and MS raised to $195 (from $175) on accelerating data center demand—Oct Q data center expected +45% QoQ/+160% YoY to potentially $200M+ quarterly run rate by F1Q28. FiberEdge 1.6T expected >50% market share by FY27 end. Gross margin structurally improving ~500bps from cellular module divestiture.

bullets.title: GLW: LCD TV panel price declines moderating; JPM maintains Neutral
bullets.body: LCD TV panel prices fell 2.7% MoM in August (17th consecutive YoY decline), but JPM expects declines to ease to 2.2% in September and stabilize in October as TV makers lift purchases ~10% QoQ from a low base. Limited 4Q26 visibility remains the overhang. Corning's Display segment covers 97% of global LCD viewing area with TVs representing 70%+ of coverage.

bullets.title: GEV: 6-day losing streak, longest since Oct 2025; WMB and KMI rated Buy by GS on data center gas demand
bullets.body: GE Vernova (GEV) on track for 6 consecutive down days, its longest streak since October 2025—historical precedent saw the stock more than double over 6 months following the prior similar episode. Separately, Goldman Sachs raised its data center natural gas demand forecast to 10-11 bcf/d by 2030 (from 7-8 bcf/d) and rates WMB and KMI as Buy as preferred pipeline beneficiaries.

bullets.title: SNDK: Below 50-day MA for 6th consecutive session; Hedgeye bearish
bullets.body: SanDisk (SNDK) closed below its 50-day moving average for a 6th straight session. The last time SNDK had multiple closes below the 50-day MA, the price declined 43% over the following two weeks. Hedgeye Risk Range flags SNDK as Bullish trend, creating a conflicting signal.

bullets.title: NBIS: Short interest surges to 26%; market calls company bluff
bullets.body: Nebius Group (NBIS) short interest has risen to 26%, with market commentary characterizing the elevated short as the market questioning the company's credibility. No specific fundamental catalyst cited in the period.

bullets.title: CRM and CRWD: Reporting tonight; Citi bullish on both ahead of print
bullets.body: Salesforce (CRM) and CrowdStrike (CRWD) both report earnings after the close today. Street consensus for CRM is $11.33B revenue / $3.27 EPS. Citi recommends buying CRWD calls ahead of earnings, citing AI OEM integration and expanding budget capture as IBM cyber procurement disruption validates demand thesis. CRWD and CRM are in the same after-close slot as NVDA.

bullets.title: DKNG: Closes $1.45B debt financing package; sports betting regulatory outlook event
bullets.body: DraftKings closed a $700M Term Loan B and $750M revolving credit facility. Morgan Stanley hosted a regulatory expert on US sports betting and iGaming legislative trends, covering state-level legalization and regulatory efforts. No directional rating change noted.
